provenance.reference: 1871 census RG10/5417; Slater's 1880; Glamorgan Gazette 14 Oct 1910 p.8; Cardiff Times 23 Apr 1910 p.10

scope.label: Not our farm
scope.reason: The census puts David Thomas at the Cowbridge Great House; our farm was the Williamses'.

detail.heading: The record
items: Glamorgan Gazette, 14 Oct 1910, p.8, under the paper's “COWBRIDGE.” heading: “Mr. David Thomas, of Great House Farm, Llandough, has just celebrated his 90th birthday.”

1871 census, RG10/5417 (Bridgend registration district, enumeration district 6, Llandough juxta Cowbridge), “Great House”: THOMAS David, Head, 50, “Farmer 140a Emp 4 Men&1 Boy”, born St Hilary. That places his birth about 1821, so he turned 90 in 1910 (transcription on FreeCEN).

Same census, our farm: RG10/5368 (Cardiff registration district, enumeration district 35, Llandough juxta Penarth), “Great House Farm”: WILLIAMS John, Head, 43, “Farmer 110 Acres, Emp 2 Men” (transcription on FreeCEN).
Slater's Directory 1880, Cowbridge section, Farmers: “IN LLANDOUGH PARISH. Morris Thomas, Llandough / Thomas David, Great House”.

Cardiff Times, 23 Apr 1910, p.10, Glamorgan puppy show: “luncheon subsequently at Mr Thomas's, Great House Farm, Llandough” (the Glamorgan Hunt kennels farm; Mr Arthur Spencer there in the Glamorgan Gazette, 3 May 1907).

Glamorgan Gazette, 27 Sep 1907 (also 4 and 11 Oct 1907): “STRAYED, to Great House Farm, Llandough … J. Thomas, Llandough” (read from search snippets only; the date is not yet confirmed from the page).

detail.heading: What it does and does not establish
detail.text: Two farms called Great House stood in two parishes called Llandough. The deciding record is the 1871 census, which places David Thomas at Llandough juxta Cowbridge and John Williams at Llandough juxta Penarth. The 1910 birthday note, the 1907 advert and the hunt reports belong to the Cowbridge farm. They say nothing about Tŷ Mawr.

detail.heading: Next step
detail.text: None for the identity question. A 1911 census copy (RG14, Llandough-juxta-Cowbridge) would add the last household, but it is not needed to decide.

provenance.reference: National Library of Wales D 219/9–13; Glamorgan Archives DB/E/1 plan 19 (EV-0211); EV-0228; EV-0233

scope.label: Separate farm
scope.reason: A separate farmstead with its own deeds: Llandough Farm, 166 acres, NLW D 219/9–13 (1824–1832), against 107 acres for Cydfin Farm or Tŷ Mawr Farm (D 219/1, 4–5, 8 et seq.). The 1824 survey plan labels Llandough Farm apart from Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm.

detail.heading: The record
items: The National Library of Wales catalogue of the Bute estate records (D 219) describes Llandough Farm (166 acres; deeds D 219/9–13, 1824–1832) separately from Cydfin Farm or Tŷ Mawr Farm (107 acres; D 219/1, 4–5, 8 et seq.).
The 1824 Stewart survey plan 19 (EV-0211) names “Llandough Farm” as its own place on the plan, beside the Village of Llandough, Wellspring and the River Ely, and apart from “Cedfin or Ty Mawr Farm”.
Llandough Farm was the Rees family farm in the 1841 tithe and in press reports from 1865 to 1910 (EV-0228).
The 1940 Western Ground Rents tenancy to David and Thomas Thomas concerns Llandough Farm (EV-0233).

detail.heading: What it does and does not establish
detail.text: A positive identity correction: the two holdings are separate in the catalogue and on the 1824 plan. “Llandough Farm” is not a name of the property, and its 166 acres, its deeds and its tenancies cannot be carried over to Tŷ Mawr because both lie in the same parish.

frogs.title: Marquess of Bute v Seymour; Marquess of Bute v White; Barry Railway Co v Seymour; Barry Railway Co v White (Llandough right of way, 1905)
frogs.place_text: Fields between the Cardiff–Sully road and Eastbrook (Green Seys / Cornerswell side), Llandough

provenance.reference: Evening Express 20, 28, 29, 31 Mar 1905; Western Mail 21, 23 Mar 1905

scope.label: Not our farm
scope.reason: Bute land on the Cornerswell side of the parish; no Williams and no Great House appears in any report.

detail.heading: The record
items: The court's view: “Mr. Justice Lawrence, sitting in the Nisi Prius Court, Cardiff, formally entered judgment for plaintiffs in the Llandough right of way dispute case, and granted an injunction in the terms asked for—restraining trespassing on the land of the Barry Railway Company and also of the Marquess of Bute, with costs.” (Evening Express, 29 Mar 1905, p.3). The special jury's verdict for the plaintiffs came on 28 Mar 1905 (Glamorgan Assizes, before Lawrence J).

The action: “they each sued each of the two defendants … for damage for trespass on June 4, 1904. The defence was that the defendants were legitimately using a public path across fields at Llandough, the property of the Marques of Bute, and across the Barry Company's line, and leading from the Cardiff and Sully road to Eastbrook.” (Evening Express, 20 Mar 1905, p.3).
Counsel for Bute (a submission, not a finding): “Between the years 1848 and 1893 there was no person who could dedicate, because the estate was in strict settlement” (Evening Express, 28 Mar 1905).

Costs “including the expense of the assize action and the previous proceedings in London” were about £2,000; the defendants' share, about £500, was raised by public subscription (Evening Express, 31 Mar 1905, p.3).
The land named: the Green Seys (“Greensays”) fields, Cornerswell Farm, Westhouse, the One Acre Field (“Erw Heol Goch”) and a field of Colonel Homfray's.

detail.heading: What it does and does not establish
detail.text: The same parish and the same landlord, Bute, but different land towards Dinas Powis. About twenty reports were read; none names Great House, Tŷ Mawr or the Williamses. Bute acting as owner of Llandough land in 1904–05 fits the Williamses being Bute's tenants.

detail.heading: Next step
detail.text: Only if family papers mention a path or trespass case: the Bute estate's own file (solicitor J. S. Corbett) in the Bute papers at Glamorgan Archives.

frogs.place_text: Western District outfall sewer (Cardiff to Lavernock, through Llandough)

provenance.reference: Evening Express 11 Jun 1906, 14 Jul 1910; Western Mail 7 Mar, 24 Oct 1912; Dublin Builder 25 May 1912

scope.label: Out of scope

detail.heading: The record
items: The arbitrator's view: Mr H. Percy Boulnois, M.Inst.C.E., “has given his award in the case of Whyte & Co., Ltd., v. Cardiff Corporation, in respect of a dispute which arose between the parties after the completion of the western [outfall sewer]” (Dublin Builder, 25 May 1912, p.28; snippet). The hearing ended at the Westminster Palace Hotel, London (Western Mail, 7 Mar 1912, p.5; snippet). The amount of the award has not been read (paywalled); the South Wales Weekly Argus of 11 May 1912 headed it “CARDIFF'S SURPRISE. Summary of the Award”.
The contract: Whyte & Co. of Belfast took Contract No. 6, Western Sewer, at £70,368 5s 4d (Evening Express, 11 Jun 1906).

The dispute: a final account of £123,452 3s 10d, “the difference of £53,083 16s. 6d. really represented extras”; the town clerk was asked “to advise the committee upon the legal questions involved” (Evening Express, 14 Jul 1910).
Afterwards a council row: Western Mail 24 Oct 1912 p.6; Western Mail 15 Jan 1913; South Wales Daily News 19 Feb 1913 p.6, “Cardiff Western Sewer. ‘NOTHING TO HIDE’” (snippets).

detail.heading: What it does and does not establish
detail.text: The only dispute found that arose from the works the 23 Feb 1905 Bute conveyance to Cardiff served (EV-0013). It is a contract arbitration, not a court judgment, and nothing read shows it went on to the High Court. Whether Contract No. 6 was the Llandough section is not known.

detail.text: A paid reading of the 1912 award reports, or Cardiff borough Public Works Committee minutes 1910–13 at Glamorgan Archives.
